paper_title: From tree matching to sparse graph alignment
statement: 3. Conclusion We have introduced NTMA, an algorithm we proved to succeed at partial alignment of sparse correlated random graphs. While our Theorem applies to a limited range of average degrees λ, we conjecture that rates γ(λ) and γ(λ, s, δ) are strictly less than λ for all λ > 1 and s < 1 and thus NTMA in fact succeeds for a much broader parameter range. This will be the object of future work.
context: Proof strategy for Theorem 2.2. Consider two distinct nodes i and u. We place ourselves on the event of high probability that BG∪ (i, 2d) has no cycle. On this event, the two neighborhoods BG1 (i, d) and BG2 (u, d) can be coupled with two trees rooted at i, u respectively. We then distinguish several cases that are shown on Figure 10, that require detailed analysis, and which all show that for i fixed, one has P (∃u 6= i, (i, u) ∈ S) = o(1). The full proof is deferred to Appendix D.5. 3. Conclusion We have introduced NTMA, an algorithm we proved to succeed at partial alignment of sparse correlated random graphs. While our Theorem applies to a limited range of average degrees λ, we conjecture that rates γ(λ) and γ(λ, s, δ) are strictly less than λ for all λ > 1 and s < 1 and thus NTMA in fact succeeds for a much broader parameter range. This will be the object of future work. 12 F ROM TREE MATCHING TO SPARSE GRAPH ALIGNMENT
